answer.rationale: Primary expires in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line sits at 94% and zero buffer, so delivery continuity dominates TCO. Incumbent renewal historically preserved integration and deliveries (c1); benchmarking/renegotiation moved price and terms (c4) and multi-year volume pricing cut unit cost without narrowing scope (c6). The low-cost quote meets the 18% mandate and last year's switch was operationally clean (c2), but a primary cutover now would raise delivery risk the objective forbids; a dual-source add would not replace the expiring contract. Deferral (c5) applied to a non-critical month-to-month service, not this expiry. Negotiate against the low-cost quote and the 18% mandate while keeping the incumbent as primary. Uncertain whether the incumbent will actually concede 18%; verifying c4 before committing to how hard that lever historically moved price.
